# A merge performed WITHOUT sesam's audit-log driver (e.g. a fresh clone before
# `sesam init` set up the local git config) forces the user to resolve the log
# conflict by hand. Taking one side wholesale drops the other side's audit
# entries - a silent truncation of the mainline. VerifyHistory's first-parent
# walk must catch it (a proper `sesam` merge rebases instead, losing nothing).

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

cp base.txt $TMPDIR/base.txt
cp theirs.txt $TMPDIR/theirs.txt

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt db.txt
exec sesam add db.txt --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add db'

# OURS: add bob - a distinctive audit entry that must survive any merge.
exec git checkout -b ours
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: tell bob'

# THEIRS: edit the secret and reseal (also changes the audit log).
exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt db.txt
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: edit+seal'

# Simulate a merge with NO sesam log driver configured: git falls back to a plain
# text merge and the audit log conflicts.
exec git checkout ours
exec git config --remove-section merge.sesam-merge-log
! exec git merge theirs
stdout 'CONFLICT'

# The user "resolves" by taking theirs wholesale - silently dropping ours'
# tell-bob entry. --no-verify skips pre-commit so nothing re-adds it.
exec git checkout --theirs .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
exec git add -A
exec git commit --no-verify --no-edit

# The dropped mainline entry is caught by the first-parent truncation check.
! exec sesam verify
stderr 'truncated'

-- base.txt --
S=BASE
-- theirs.txt --
S=THEIRS
